channel.title: The Nile Pen
channel.description: Independent voices on climate justice, South Sudan politics and human rights. For Africans, the diaspora and everyone paying attention.

item.title: Nearly 90 million displaced people face severe climate risks, UNHCR warns ahead of COP31
item.description: UNHCR said three in four forcibly displaced people live in countries with high to extreme exposure to climate hazards.

item.title: South Sudan hosts more than 1.3 million people fleeing Sudan's war
item.description: Latest figures show South Sudan is the second-largest destination for people fleeing Sudan, after Egypt.

item.title: UK funding helps South Sudan act before El Niño shocks hit
item.description: New UK support lets FAO and WFP run anticipatory flood interventions in Jonglei, Unity and Upper Nile, reaching at-risk households before floods strike.

item.title: Five killed as rival SPLA-IO forces clash in Leer
item.description: Fighting between rival factions of the SPLA-IO in Leer County left five people dead and nine injured, according to local reports.

item.title: SPLM official missing after reported arrest in Kapoeta
item.description: An SPLM official is missing following a reported arrest in Kapoeta, separately from reports of two youths detained in Kapoeta South whose whereabouts are unknown.

item.title: Egypt and Sudan invoke colonial-era Nile agreement in renewed GERD challenge
item.description: In a joint statement, Cairo and Khartoum demanded a binding legal framework for the dam's operation, describing their water security as “indivisible”.

item.title: Academics say December elections are unlikely, citing legal and administrative hurdles
item.description: Scholars point to unresolved legal and administrative steps, including the absence of a census and voter roll, as reasons the December vote may not go ahead as planned.

item.title: One killed, three injured in clashes near South Sudan–Uganda border
item.description: A clash near the border with Uganda left one person dead and three injured, according to Eye Radio.

item.title: “I was forced into marriage at the age of 14”: a feature on child marriage
item.description: A first-person feature from Rumbek on child marriage and its lasting consequences for girls.

item.title: Civil society forum says South Sudan is not ready for elections
item.description: A civil society forum warned that the conditions for a credible vote are not yet in place, adding to calls for safeguards before polling day.

item.title: South Sudanese children demand climate action as floods threaten their future
item.description: Children called on the government and world leaders to move beyond pledges and protect education, health and livelihoods from floods, drought and extreme heat.

item.title: UN Commission urges General Assembly to act collectively for lasting peace in South Sudan
item.description: The UN Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan called on the General Assembly to take urgent, collective action to secure lasting peace.

item.title: Nearly 2.4 million South Sudanese are refugees — most of them children
item.description: USA for UNHCR reports nearly 2.4 million South Sudanese refugees and 3.5 million forcibly displaced people overall. 56 per cent of refugees are under 18.

item.title: South Sudan summons Sudan's envoy over deadly Abyei drone attack
item.description: Juba summoned Khartoum's ambassador following the drone strike on the Abyei market, raising diplomatic tension between the two neighbours.

item.title: How Sudan's shift to drone warfare is fuelling a civilian crisis
item.description: A look at how drones have become a central weapon in Sudan's war, and how the attacks are reaching markets and civilians, including in the border region shared with South Sudan.

item.title: Drone strike on Abyei market kills more than 150, officials say
item.description: South Sudanese officials said drone strikes hit a market in the disputed Abyei region, killing more than 150 people in one of the deadliest attacks of the war that has spilled across Sudan's borders.

item.title: Civil society blames political interference for worsening communal violence
item.description: South Sudanese civil society groups say political interference is driving worsening communal violence across the country.

item.title: Sudanese TPS holders in the US get a temporary reprieve
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security said Sudanese TPS holders keep their status for now, with a decision to be made “at the appropriate time”.

item.title: The GERD dispute explained: what Ethiopia built and where Sudan stands
item.description: An explainer on Africa's largest hydropower dam, opened in September 2025, and the stalled negotiations.

item.title: South Sudan launches $267 million project to import power from Uganda
item.description: The government has launched a $267 million project to bring electricity from Uganda, aimed at easing chronic power shortages.

item.title: South Sudan shortens academic calendar ahead of elections
item.description: Education authorities have shortened the school year ahead of the planned December elections.

item.title: September brought widespread rainfall deficits and above-average heat
item.description: NOAA's monthly climate summary recorded widespread drier-than-normal conditions and above-average temperatures across South Sudan in September.

item.title: Intercommunal clashes kill 71 people in South Sudan
item.description: At least 71 people were killed in intercommunal fighting, adding to a year of rising local violence as the country heads towards elections.

item.title: South Sudan's aid crisis deepens as food stocks run low
item.description: Humanitarian food stocks are running low as families continue to arrive in border towns such as Renk after fleeing the war in Sudan.

item.title: Bentiu's dykes under strain from El Niño and funding cuts
item.description: Temporary dykes protecting Bentiu, maintained by IOM and UNMISS, face heavy pressure from rainfall, El Niño and humanitarian funding cuts.

item.title: Analysis: President jettisons unity government and hardens grip on power
item.description: Crisis Group sees two likely paths after the government's dissolution: a stage-managed vote without a census or voter roll, or a late postponement that extends the president's term.

item.title: With GERD complete, the harder problem begins
item.description: All 13 turbines are now operating and the dam was confirmed complete in February 2026, but no binding treaty is in place.

item.title: Kiir dissolves government ahead of first national elections
item.description: President Salva Kiir dissolved the unity government formed under the 2018 peace deal, months before the country's first national elections since independence.

item.title: UN investigators warn of growing risks to civilians and the democratic transition
item.description: After its 14th visit to the country, the UN Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan said renewed violence, political tensions, shrinking civic space, entrenched corruption and persistent impunity are putting civilians and the transition at risk.

item.title: Men deported from the US to Juba remain held in guarded complex
item.description: Five of eight men forcibly sent to South Sudan in July 2025 remain detained in a guarded complex in Juba as of September 2026, according to a monitoring group.

item.title: Opinion: South Sudan cannot be governed through fear, division and perpetual transition
item.description: A human rights lawyer argues the December elections must be a real exercise of citizens' rights rather than a ceremony to legitimise those already in power.

item.title: Ethiopia says it needs no permission for Nile projects as Sudan reports inflow drop
item.description: Ethiopia's water minister rejected joint management of the GERD and defended Ethiopia's right to equitable use of the Nile.

item.title: Opinion: South Sudan needs fiscal discipline and stronger governance
item.description: An op-ed arguing that economic stability depends on tighter control of public finances and stronger institutions.

item.title: Opinion: The PPC under public scrutiny — what next for political parties?
item.description: A commentary on the Political Parties Council and the state of party politics ahead of the vote.

item.title: After GERD, can Egypt shape Ethiopia's next Nile dams?
item.description: Ethiopia has announced plans for further Blue Nile projects, a new test for Egypt after it failed to prevent the GERD.

item.title: Elections without safeguards could fuel renewed conflict, UN Commission warns
item.description: In its advisory “At the Brink”, the Commission said the safeguards needed for a peaceful, credible vote are largely absent as South Sudan moves towards its first national elections.

item.title: Armed raid on cattle camp kills at least 49
item.description: At least 49 people were killed in an armed raid on a cattle camp, part of a wider pattern of violence linked to cattle and grazing land.

item.title: TPS for South Sudanese in the US ends after court ruling
item.description: A federal judge allowed the administration to end Temporary Protected Status for South Sudanese nationals, which had let hundreds live and work in the United States.

item.title: What the end of TPS means for South Sudanese in the US
item.description: TPS status and TPS work permits for South Sudan are no longer valid. People without another legal status risk detention and removal proceedings.

item.title: Analysis: stability deteriorated and risk of war rose in the second quarter
item.description: Janes assesses that unilateral amendments to the 2018 peace agreement in April raised the risk of a return to war, with army integration still stalled.

item.title: Civilians flee abuses by government forces and allies in Western Equatoria
item.description: Human Rights Watch reported that many residents of Nagero County fled after attacks by government forces and allied groups.

item.title: Opinion: Can the December elections build a politics of peace, service and accountability?
item.description: Alexander Makuach Kuol argues the vote could open a new chapter only as part of a wider national covenant for peace, inclusion and economic recovery.

item.title: Analysis: UN cash crunch and narrower mandate weaken civilian protection
item.description: The Global Centre for R2P notes base closures and troop repatriations under the UN liquidity crisis, and an April Security Council decision that reduced the mission's direct support for elections.

item.title: “Super El Niño” deepens hunger crisis, WFP says
item.description: The World Food Programme warned that a very strong El Niño is worsening an already severe hunger crisis in South Sudan.

item.title: The Forgotten Floods: How South Sudan's Wetlands Are Disappearing
item.description: Across the Sudd basin, communities are watching the land they have farmed for generations drain away. This is not just an ecological crisis — it is a political one.

item.title: Drought, Debt and Displacement: Who Owes What to East Africa's Climate Refugees?
item.description: As climate-induced migration reshapes the Horn of Africa, a new generation of legal scholars and activists are making the case that historical emissions must come with reparations — and they are bringing that argument to international courts.

item.title: UN acts ahead of drought to protect thousands
item.description: UN agencies released support in advance of forecast drought conditions to protect vulnerable households.

item.title: What the Juba Negotiations Actually Mean for Ordinary Citizens
item.description: Beyond the diplomatic language, the stakes for South Sudanese families remain urgent and largely unaddressed.

item.title: Press Freedom in the Nile Basin: A Shrinking Space
item.description: Journalists across the region are navigating detention, censorship, and self-censorship — yet independent reporting persists.

item.title: From Kampala to London: How the South Sudanese Diaspora is Funding Change
item.description: Remittances and advocacy networks are increasingly influential in shaping both policy and community resilience back home.

item.title: The Nile Agreement That Wasn't: Unpacking the GERD Standoff
item.description: As Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam shifts the region's power balance, downstream nations face a future of uncertainty and negotiation.

item.title: Thousands on the brink of famine, WFP warns
item.description: WFP said thousands of people in South Sudan are on the brink of famine as conflict, displacement and climate shocks combine.

item.title: New project to rehabilitate water infrastructure and cut flood risk
item.description: UNOPS and the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation will implement a World Bank-financed resilience project in Eastern Equatoria, Jonglei, Lakes and Upper Nile.

item.title: Funding gaps threaten nearly 2 million displaced people
item.description: IOM warned that shortfalls in funding put support for nearly 2 million displaced people in South Sudan at risk.

item.title: Commentary: Don't diminish the UN peacekeeping mission in South Sudan
item.description: Human Rights Watch argues that cutting back UNMISS would leave civilians more exposed at a dangerous moment.

item.title: Opinion: South Sudan's 2026 elections are a test the country is not yet ready to pass
item.description: The writer argues the structural conditions that once turned political competition into ethnic violence have not been addressed, including the army's ties to the ruling party and the delayed hybrid court.

item.title: Egypt and Ethiopia: is a Nile conflict looming?
item.description: An analysis of the water and agricultural pressures facing Egypt and Sudan as the GERD reaches full operation.

item.title: South Sudan's refugees escaped war — then came the funding cuts
item.description: WFP describes how funding cuts are reducing assistance for refugees who have already fled conflict.

item.title: The Nile dam standoff heats up as Washington re-enters the dispute
item.description: In January the US told Egypt it was renewing efforts to resolve the dispute with Ethiopia, adding a new layer to an already tense regional picture.

item.title: UN inquiry: leaders are dismantling the 2018 peace deal and risking full-scale war
item.description: Presenting its report to the Human Rights Council, the Commission said political and military leaders are systematically dismantling the Revitalized Peace Agreement, exposing civilians to grave risks of renewed armed conflict and mass atrocity crimes.

item.title: Diaspora remittances remain a lifeline for social support networks
item.description: The BTI 2026 country report notes that the South Sudanese diaspora, with large communities in the US, UK, Canada and Australia, plays a significant role in supporting families through remittances.

item.title: World Report: no progress on the Hybrid Court as rights situation deteriorates
item.description: Human Rights Watch's World Report says South Sudan's human rights situation significantly deteriorated amid escalating political violence, and that no action was taken to establish the Hybrid Court.

item.title: Abductions and sexual violence rise even as overall incidents fall, UNMISS says
item.description: The UN mission documented 295 incidents of conflict-related violence affecting 1,153 civilians in its quarterly brief.

item.title: Abusive “anti-gang” crackdown brings mass arbitrary arrests, says HRW
item.description: Human Rights Watch documented mass arbitrary arrests, ill-treatment, rape and forced conscription, including of boys, during a security campaign framed as a crackdown on gangs.

item.title: Opinion: South Sudan is not ready to hold elections in 2026
item.description: The piece argues most core provisions of the 2018 peace agreement remain unfulfilled, and that holding elections without addressing them risks a return to instability.
